perspective:
From Harold Padilla’s subjective perspective, he has access to:

- He is a project manager. He feels frustrated and anxious because his project team seems unmotivated, which is affecting project progress.
- He knows Arthur Begum as a police officer and friend he relies on for advice. Harold arranged and attended a coffee-shop meeting with Arthur.
- Harold told Arthur his team seemed completely unmotivated and that he was at his wit’s end. Arthur asked if he had tried understanding what drives each team member individually. Harold admitted he had focused mainly on goals/deadlines, then considered looking into personal motivations. Arthur advised one-on-one conversations and making people feel valued/understood. Harold decided to try it and felt more hopeful.
- Harold later felt hopeful and relieved. He told his team he wanted quick one-on-one chats to understand what motivates each of them. He heard Team Member 1 say that could be helpful and Team Member 2 say they were open to it. Harold said he would schedule time with each person.
- Harold noticed the team still was not responding well to the new strategies. He felt disappointed and worried about the project’s future. He told Arthur he had tried the suggestions but the team still was not responding. Arthur suggested deeper issues such as personal conflicts, lack of trust, or external stressors, and advised digging deeper. Harold agreed to set up another round of meetings.
- In those one-on-one meetings, Harold said he had noticed performance issues and asked for concerns. Team Member 1 told him there was tension between a few team members affecting their work. Team Member 2 told him they felt overwhelmed by the workload and stressed, making motivation hard. Harold said he would look into resolving conflicts and try to redistribute tasks to ease pressure, and that their well-being mattered.
- Harold felt optimistic and empowered, believing that addressing individual concerns would improve performance. He told the team he would implement regular feedback sessions and team-building activities to create a more supportive environment. He heard Team Member 1 say that sounded great and Team Member 2 agree that their concerns were being addressed. Harold said he was glad and wanted to work together to make the project a success.

Harold does **not** have access to other characters’ private thoughts, unspoken motives, narrator-only descriptions, or information not heard/observed by him.
